steps.say: The practice house! Electricity makes lights and toasters work. It can hurt, so it stays inside wires and machines. Some things here are dangerous: let's find them.

lines.hz_dryer_bath: A hair dryer by the bath: water and electricity must never meet.
lines.hz_drink_socket: A drink by the socket: a spill could reach the electricity.
lines.hz_frayed: A cable with its wires showing: don't touch it.
lines.hz_overload: Too many plugs in one socket: it can get too hot.
lines.hz_fork_toaster: A fork in the toaster: never poke anything into a toaster.
lines.hz_socket_toy: A toy key by the socket: nothing goes into a socket but a plug.
lines.hz_kite: A kite in the power lines: never fly a kite near them.

steps.say: Your hands are wet from washing. You want to switch on the light. First...

choices.text: Switch it on with wet hands
choices.why: Water and electricity never mix: dry your hands first.

steps.done: Dry hands first, every time.

steps.say: What goes into a socket?

choices.why: Never poke anything into a socket: only plugs go in.

steps.done: Only plugs. And grown-ups plug in the big things.

steps.say: Your kite gets stuck in the power lines. You...

choices.text: Leave it and tell a grown-up

choices.why: Never pull it or climb for it: leave it and tell a grown-up.

steps.done: Leave it: grown-ups call the power company to get it.

steps.say: Well spotted! Dry hands, only plugs in sockets, far from power lines, and tell a grown-up about a danger.

name_it.title: Spot it, keep away, tell
lines: Water and electricity never mix: dry hands, and nothing electric by the bath.
Nothing goes into a socket but a plug.
A damaged cable or too many plugs: don't touch, tell a grown-up.
Stay far away from power lines.
name_it.source: Electrical Safety First and its Switched On Kids, and the fire and rescue services

little.try_real: With a grown-up, go round your home and find the sockets. Is anything wet nearby, a cable damaged, too many plugs in one? Show them what you found.

sources.fact: Keep electrical items away from water, and never touch plugs, switches or appliances with wet hands.
sources.source: Electrical Safety First, Switched On Kids

sources.fact: Never put anything into a socket or a toaster except what is meant to go there; unplug a toaster before getting stuck bread out.
Never fly kites near overhead power lines, and never try to get one back if it is caught: tell an adult, who calls the power company.
sources.source: Energy Networks Association (the UK's electricity networks), safety

steps.say: The practice house and the practice park. Today: water and electricity, plugs and cables, sockets, and power lines outside.

safe_mistake.wrong: using a hair dryer with wet hands
safe_mistake.why: Water lets electricity through, and through you: wet hands on a plug or a switch can give you a shock.
safe_mistake.right: Dry your hands first, then use it.

steps.say: You've had a bath and your hands are still wet. You want to dry your hair. What do you do first?
steps.done: Dry hands first: water and electricity never mix.

not.bath_edge: Not by the bath: if it fell into the water, the electricity would be in the water too.

steps.say: Where does the hair dryer go while you use it?
steps.done: Far from the bath and the basin.

not.bath_edge: Not by the bath: if it fell into the water, the electricity would be in the water too.

steps.say: Where does the hair dryer go while you use it?
steps.done: Far from water, all by yourself.

not.cable: Not by the cable: pulling it can break the wires inside. Hold the plug itself.

steps.say: All done: switch off and unplug it. Hold the plug, not the cable.
steps.done: By the plug's head: the cable stays safe.

not.frayed_cable: Never touch a damaged cable: the bare wires can give you a shock. Tell a grown-up.

steps.say: Look at the lamp's cable: the wires inside are showing. What do you do?
steps.done: Gus switches it off at the socket, unplugs it and puts it away to be mended.

steps.say: This socket has an adaptor plugged into an adaptor, full of plugs. Bobo wants to plug in a heater too.

choices.text: No: tell a grown-up. Never an adaptor in an adaptor

choices.why: Too many plugs can make a socket overheat and start a fire. Tell a grown-up.

steps.done: Gus spreads the plugs out: one adaptor at most, and never a heater on one.

steps.say: Now the practice park. See the power lines on their tall poles: they carry a lot of electricity.

not.near_lines: Too near the power lines. Fly kites in an open field, far from them.

steps.say: Where is a safe place to fly a kite?
steps.done: An open field, far from power lines.

not.near_lines: Too near the power lines. Fly kites in an open field, far from them.

steps.say: Where is a safe place to fly a kite?
steps.done: Far from the power lines: you chose by yourself.

steps.say: Oh! A gust blows Pip-pop's kite into the power lines. What now?

choices.text: Let go, leave it and tell a grown-up
Pull the string to get it back
choices.why: Never pull it or climb for it: a string near the lines can carry electricity. Leave it.

steps.done: A grown-up calls the power company: they get it down safely.

steps.say: Bobo wants to climb the tree under the power lines.

choices.text: Not that tree: never climb near power lines

choices.why: Branches can touch the lines, and electricity can jump across. Climb only trees far from power lines.

steps.done: Trees far from the lines only.

not.substation_gate: Never go in, not even for a ball: a substation is full of electricity. Tell a grown-up.

steps.say: Your ball went over the fence with the yellow DANGER sign. That's a substation. What do you do?
steps.done: Gus calls the number on the sign: the power company gets it out safely.

not.substation_gate: Never go in, not even for a ball: a substation is full of electricity. Tell a grown-up.

steps.say: Your ball went over the substation's fence. What do you do?
steps.done: You told a grown-up: the power company gets it out.

name_it.title: Water, plugs, power lines
lines: Water and electricity never mix: dry hands, and keep electric things away from water.
Unplug by the plug, not the cable. A damaged cable: don't touch it, tell a grown-up.
One adaptor at most: never an adaptor in an adaptor.
Stay far from power lines and substations: never fly kites or climb near them.
name_it.source: Electrical Safety First, and the electricity network companies' safety advice

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: check the sockets at home for adaptors and too many plugs, and find the power lines near your park, so you know where never to fly a kite.

sources.fact: Water and electricity don't mix: keep appliances away from water and never use them with wet hands.
Don't overload sockets: avoid plugging an adaptor into an adaptor, and use one bar adaptor per socket at most; high-power appliances like heaters go straight into a wall socket.
Pull out a plug by holding the plug, never by tugging the cable; stop using damaged cables and plugs.
Stay away from overhead lines and substations: never fly kites or climb trees near them, and never enter a substation for a ball or a pet; call the number on the sign.

big.twist: The main switch and the safe place don't glow: you choose by yourself.

steps.say: The practice house, for older helpers: the fuse box and its RCD, someone stuck to electricity, and a fallen power line after a storm. This is practice. A real first aid course teaches more.
This is the fuse box. Every home has one, and it matters to know where it is. Touch its cover.
steps.done: The fuse box: its main switch turns all the power in the house off.

steps.say: A grown-up tests the RCD, the safety switch. Press its test button, marked T.
steps.done: Click! It switched itself off: it works. An RCD switches off fast if electricity goes the wrong way, like through a person.

steps.say: Now switch the RCD back on.
steps.done: On again. Its label says how often to test it: often every three months.

steps.say: A plug's case is cracked, and the cable is loose where it goes in.

choices.text: Stop using it: a grown-up gets it mended or replaced

choices.why: Tape doesn't make it safe: a damaged plug or cable needs mending or replacing.

steps.done: Unplugged and put away until it's mended.

steps.say: Practice time. Gus was mending a lamp that was still plugged in. Now he is stuck to the electricity and can't let go. Stay calm: the coach is here.

safe_mistake.why: The electricity would go through you too, and then two people would be stuck.
safe_mistake.right: Never touch them. Switch the power off at the fuse box if you can reach it safely; if not, shout for a grown-up and call {number}.

steps.say: The fuse box is close by in the hall, and nothing near it is wet. What do you do?
steps.done: The main switch is off: the electricity stopped. Grown-ups do just this, when they can reach it safely.

safe_mistake.why: The electricity would go through you too, and then two people would be stuck.
safe_mistake.right: Never touch them. Switch the power off at the fuse box if you can reach it safely; if not, shout for a grown-up and call {number}.

steps.say: Gus is stuck to the electricity. What do you do?
steps.done: Power off, without touching him: all by yourself.

steps.say: Now call {number}: someone hurt by electricity always needs a doctor. Pick up the phone.
steps.done: Phone in your hand.

steps.done: Calling. Say what happened and where.

steps.say: The power is off and help is coming. Now?

choices.text: Stay with him; cool any burn with cool water
Switch the power back on to check

steps.say: After a storm, the practice park's path: a power line lies on the ground. It may still be live, and the ground around it too.

safe_mistake.wrong: going closer to look at a fallen power line
safe_mistake.why: Electricity can spread through the ground around a fallen line: even standing near it is not safe.
safe_mistake.right: Stay at least 10 metres away, and keep others away.

steps.done: Far away from it: at least 10 metres, more if you can.

name_it.title: Fuse box, stuck, fallen line
lines: Know where the fuse box is: its main switch turns all the power off. A grown-up tests the RCD.
Someone stuck to electricity: never touch them. Switch off at the fuse box if you safely can, and call {number}.
A fallen power line: stay at least 10 metres away, keep others away, call {number}.
Damaged plugs and cables: stop using them until a grown-up gets them mended.
name_it.source: Electrical Safety First, St John Ambulance and the British Red Cross (electric shock first aid), and the electricity network companies

big.try_real: With a grown-up, find your home's fuse box and its main switch. Watch them test the RCD's button, and talk about what you'd do if you saw a fallen power line.

sources.fact: Know where your fuse box (consumer unit) is; an RCD switches off quickly if there is a fault, and its test button should be pressed regularly (the label often says quarterly).
Electric shock: don't touch the person while they are in contact with the electricity; switch off the power at the mains if you can do so safely, then call 999 or 112.
Electric shock: break the contact by switching off the power if you can reach it easily, then call for help; never touch someone still in contact with it.

Fallen power lines can still be live, or come back on without warning, and the ground around them too: stay well away and keep others away; call the emergency number (and 105 in the UK). UK Power Networks and BC Hydro say at least 10 metres; the Energy Networks Association at least 5 metres (the game teaches the more careful 10).
sources.source: UK Power Networks, safety; the Energy Networks Association; BC Hydro, safe distance
